mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 3 months indicates an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises by >0.2pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A rising Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with a low inflation rate (CPIAUCSL YoY < 3.5%) signals a central bank successfully tightening without causing a recession, which typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL YoY < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high GDP growth and low unemployment), a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening demand for residential construction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods (as defined by GDPC1 growth > 2% and UNRATE < 4%), SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (the 2017 base) over the past 3 months signals a contraction in manufacturing and services, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO falls below 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly employment growth rate (PAYEMS) below 0.5% signals a slowing labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate falls below 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where PAYEMS growth is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past 3 months indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where RSAFS has increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%.
